note: Context engineering: what this study read before building, and what it took from each. Org-wide rule (Evan, 2026-10-23 13:55Z): every study lists its Oracle consultation, game dev and game design blogs and tutorials.

items.took: Comic ink family: banded light, inverted-hull outlines, hand-painted surface. Its lesson, outline width follows distance, is how the ink shell thins here.

items.t: Rendering study and the Shaders article
items.took: The toon set every look picks from (Sunday Toon, Ink, Clay as the cheap half of Storybook).
Two flat swatches per part (lit and shaded) instead of painted light; the pushed-out back-face shell for ink.
Warm terminator band and wrap light for clay skin: the Clay light here.
The rigged Meshy brutes, their 20-bone skeleton, walk and paint, reused as is.

items.t: Junya Motomura, Guilty Gear Xrd's Art Style (GDC 2015)
items.took: Hard lit/shaded threshold, flat colour per part, outlines from an inverted hull: the Saturday Action recipe.

items.t: Arc System Works, Guilty Gear toon line control
items.took: Outline shells need smoothed normals or they crack at hard edges; the shell now averages normals first.

items.t: American Cinematographer, A Textured World (Curse of the Were-Rabbit)
items.took: Aardman keeps the thumbprints and tool marks on purpose; the Plasticine look prints them into colour and bump.
Hand marks are the charm; never smooth them away.
Banded light from a few-texel ramp; we patch three's own physical material instead, so normal maps and sheen keep working.

items.t: Unity Toon Shader: base, 1st and 2nd shade colours
items.took: Per-part base and shade colours, which is how each look's part colours and posterised shading are set.
